Afghanistan Income Tax Law 2009 (unofficial translation, Official Gazette 976, 18 March 2009), art. 3: the tax year is the solar (Hejiri Shamsi) year, 1 Hamal (21 March) to the last day of Hoot (20 March)
Islamic Republic of Afghanistan Ministry of Finance: Tax Overview for Businesses, Investors & Individuals (solar taxation year; business receipts tax; no VAT)

caveats: Non-Gregorian tax year (grade P, Income Tax Law 2009, art. 3): the tax year is the solar (Hejiri Shamsi) year starting 1 Hamal (21 March) and ending the last day of Hoot (20 March). The Gregorian dates are the law's own translation; the solar year drifts against the Gregorian calendar.
companyYearEndDefault of 20 March follows the solar tax year (grade P, same article); a legal person may apply to the Ministry of Finance to use a different twelve-month year.

Afghanistan levies no VAT or GST (grade S): a narrow Business Receipts Tax and a 2% fixed business tax exist under the Income Tax Manual, but no general consumption tax (nomad.watch's reading of the MoF law; the Ministry's own overview guide).
